title: Shared Database Tables for Different Domains (Single Table Inheritance Abuse)
pattern: Mapping entirely separate domain objects to a single shared table because they share some fields, leading to lots of null columns and conditional checks.
why_bad: Couples separate concepts at the persistence level. Changes to Person attributes (e.g., adding middle name) pollute the Company record layout, making validation logic fragile.
detection: A database schema mapping containing a high count of mutually exclusive nullable columns controlled by a "type" discriminator column.
counterexample: Small tables with 95% overlapping fields where separation provides no performance or logical benefit.
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture*, "Single Table Inheritance", p. 278.
